Hi Sara — attaching our latest redline (v3) and a proposed payment schedule. A few things we want to confirm up front so legal and finance can align:

- Which legal entity will ACME accept invoices to (Acme Corp US vs Acme Global)? We need the exact remit-to for invoicing.
- Your preferred net terms (you mentioned net 30 on the call; we need to confirm or propose net 45 due to the committed credit).
- VAT / withholding responsibility by country (we've left tax clause as "customer responsible for local VAT" but happy to add evidence requirement).
- Any mandatory PO format or PO number requirement for payment processing.

Quick ask: can you review the redline and confirm the invoice entity + whether ACME requires invoices to show tax IDs? If we get those, finance can provide a clean invoice path.

Attachments: ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (PDF, tracked redlines), payment_schedule.xlsx (proposed tranche schedule)

Thanks — cc'ing Lauren and Ben for commercial/finance context.

Jordan — thanks for sending. Quick read and initial comments:

- We will route invoices to "Acme Corporation (US)" (EIN 12-3456789). I asked AP whether they require tax IDs on the invoice and they said yes.
- Net terms: Procurement prefers net 45 for new vendors; accounts payable can push for net 30 only if we get a 30-day early-pay discount or a credit reference. Can you confirm if Redwood can do net 30 with proof of credit / trade ref?
- VAT/withholding: for US dealings it's straightforward; for EU usage there will likely be VAT reverse-charge rules. We'll need Redwood to accept tax evidence (VAT registration) before issuing invoices that claim reverse-charge.
- PO: We will generate a PO after legal signs off, and it will contain an ACME PO number that AP requires on the invoice.

I attached our internal procurement notes (I put the page number where they call out the PO requirement). We are also marking the redlines in Track Changes and will send a formal redline back by EOD tomorrow.

Regards,

Thanks Sara — appreciate the quick reply. To answer your net-term question:

- We can accept net 30 for the initial 12-month commitment if ACME agrees to a 10% advance payment on the first tranche (applied to month 1) or provides two trade references. Otherwise standard offer is net 45 for new public-sector or enterprise customers.
- On PO: a PO number on the invoice is fine. If AP needs the invoice routed to a different billing entity (e.g., Acme Corporation vs Acme Cloud Solutions), Ben here will confirm the canonical remit-to and ensure the invoice template includes required fields (PO number, EIN, VAT ID fields).

Ben — can you confirm whether we can show a VAT ID on invoices and accept a PO-based workflow for ACME? Also, if we do a 10% advance, can we issue a pro-forma invoice and then follow with subsequent monthly invoices for usage?

Jordan — I’ll coordinate the commercial redline response and propose a short mutual action plan to get legal/finance through sign-off in 5 business days.

Cheers,

On Sat, Aug 7, 2027 at 9:12 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sara — attaching our latest redline (v3) and a proposed payment schedule...

Quick legal comments after reading v3 (high level):

1) Tax clause: replace the current sentence with: "Customer shall be responsible for all applicable taxes, duties and withholdings arising from the payments for the Services, excluding taxes based on Redwood's net income. Customer shall provide valid tax evidence (e.g., VAT registration) prior to any invoice that asserts tax exemption or reverse charge treatment." That requires ACME to provide evidence; please flag if procurement won't accept that.

2) Invoice entity: we should avoid tying revenue recognition to the invoice remit-to entity if ACME requests a different legal entity. Instead propose a single Redwood billing entity (Redwood Inference, Inc., EIN 98-7654321) and allow invoice remittance to a different account if AP requires it, with accounting notification. This keeps our recognition clean.

3) Late payment interest: propose 1.5% per month (18% APR) capped at local usury limits; if Procurement pushes back, we can lower to 1% per month but need a cap clause.

4) PO requirement: acceptable to require a PO number for AP processing, but do not make PO a condition precedent to payment unless Acme is a public sector entity. Suggested compromise: invoices referencing a PO will be paid per terms; failure to provide a PO delays payment processing but does not void the obligation.

I will draft precise language and add to the redline PDF; Jordan, please include my PDF in the next version to Sara.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Sara / team — thanks for the notes. A few finance items to close out so we can prepare DocuSign and invoice flow: 

- Remit-to: Redwood Inference, Inc. (EIN 98-7654321). Wire instructions and ACH details will be provided on the final invoice. We can also accept invoices routed to "Acme Corporation (US)" remit as a courtesy if AP requires, but Redwood's billing entity will remain as above for contract purposes.
- VAT / tax IDs: we can populate the invoice with a VAT ID field; if ACME claims reverse-charge, please send VAT registration (PDF) to invoices@redwood.com before first invoice.
- Net terms & advance: we can do net 30 if ACME provides either (a) two trade references or (b) 10% advance payment on first invoice. If ACME opts for the 10% advance, we will issue a pro-forma invoice with payment link (we can provide DocuSign + Stripe/ACH).
- PO: please ensure the ACME PO number is included in the "PO#" field on the invoice. If a PO is missing, we will still process the payment but it may be routed to collections for manual PO verification and delay processing by up to 10 business days.

I have prepared a short checklist and will upload final invoices and wire instructions once the redline is agreed. DocuSign envelope is ready: https://www.docusign.net/acme/orderform/12345

Thanks — Ben Carter
